page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine belonging to the g2 server family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon CPU with 8 dedicated vCPUs, consisting of 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The processor is equipped with a 38 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core.

This server includes a bundled NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 22 GB of dedicated VRAM. It does not include any local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes. There are zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included with this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance trade-off between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The CPU exhibits weak single-core and multi-core performance in Geekbench and stress-ng tests, falling into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, single-threaded compression and decompression tasks register in the lower performance tier. However, the system achieves top-tier performance in LLM inference benchmarks, processing 2225.82 tokens per second for prompt processing and 52.31 tokens per second for text generation on medium 7B models. Memory bandwidth and database operations perform in the average tier.

Given the hardware profile, the g2-standard-8 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that can offload computation to the NVIDIA L4 GPU, offsetting the weaker CPU performance. It is highly optimized for machine learning inference, specifically small to medium language model execution. It is also suitable for average-demand database operations and web serving, though it is less optimal for CPU-heavy compilation or raw single-threaded processing.
